# Binary payload and release field vectors

Hex strings are entire synthetic payloads, with no envelope. The full hex
for each row follows the table. Except where mutated, expected artifact,
owner, recovery, coordinator, filter and runtime-inventory digests are
32 repeats of `11`, `22`, `33`, `44`, `55`, `66` respectively.
The original session raw bytes are `ccddeeffaabb88997766554433221100`
in existing .NET GUID byte order. Protocol constants are all 1. The
independently expected profile is `ae4-linux-fixed-fixture-v1` / `1`.
Acceptance refers to isolated shape and content agreement in the stated
context, with caller transport and authentication supplied separately.

W13 is a syntactically valid negative confirmation and permits no
positive progression. IE-V10 deliberately repeats IE-V02 with a legacy
decoder selection. The rest of the IE bytes and expectations reproduce
the normative owner witnesses. No frame or native behavior is exercised.

## Release field only

F2 §5 and AB line 34 specify the same SHA-256 preimage. For this
downstream field witness use digest slots of 32 repeats of hex
`11`, `22`, `33`, `44`, the LE action index `02000000`, GUID
slots of 16 repeats of `55`, `66`, `77`, `88` (already in wire
byte order), and a manifest digest of 32 repeats of `99`
preceded by the ASCII domain and one zero separator as in candidate §5.
The exact computed preimage and digest are below. R01 is the expected
32 raw byte value in the existing ReleaseRequest approval-correlation
field, with the existing approval indication true. R02 changes its first
byte only. E-6 rejects the mismatch. Both are field-only witnesses.
E-3 has no ReleaseRequest serialization or validation duty.
